newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra sees 13,000 more job cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra sees 13,000 more job cuts.

text.p: Australian government-owned telecommunications firm Telstra Corp Ltd said on Friday it planned to further staff cuts of 13,000 on top of the already announced 9,000 staff cuts planned for the current year.
Telstra chief executive Frank Blount told a news conference the company expected a reduction in staff numbers of 6,000 in the year to June 30, 1998 and further 7,000 in 1998/99.
Telstra announced cuts of 9,000 for 1996/97 in July. It currently has a workforce of about 74,000.
"We anticipate that after the current financial year, staff numbers will reduce by some 6,000 in 1997/98 and allow 7,000 more in 1998/99," Blount said.
He said the total cost of redundancies would amount to A$1.1 billion, for which the company would make provision in its 1996/97 half year accounts.
Blount said that staff costs represented about 60 percent of Telstra's total costs after depreciation and direct variable costs.
Blount said that the company had implemented steep cost control measures during 1995/96 which had started to take effect towards the end of that financial year.
"Those actions will continue to impact positively on productivity and our profits for some time in the future," he said.
